papers.title: Universals in the Content and Structure of Values: Theoretical Advances and Empirical Tests in 20 Countries
papers.abstract_snippet: Foundational theory identifying 10 motivationally distinct value types recognized across cultures. Values form a circular structure reflecting compatible and conflicting motivations. Empirical tests in 20 countries with two organizing dimensions. Defines values as trans-situational goals serving as guiding principles.

papers.title: Refining the Theory of Basic Individual Values
papers.authors: Shalom H. Schwartz, Jan Cieciuch, Michele Vecchione, Eldad Davidov, Ronald Fischer, Constanze Beierlein, Alice Ramos, Markku Verkasalo, Jan-Erik Lonnqvist, Kursad Demirutku, Ozlem Dirilen-Gumus, Mark Konty
papers.venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
papers.abstract_snippet: Proposes a refined theory of 19 values on a motivational continuum, providing greater heuristic and explanatory power than the original 10 values. Confirmatory factor and multidimensional scaling analyses support discrimination of the 19 values and predict their motivational order.

papers.title: Measuring the Refined Theory of Individual Values in 49 Cultural Groups: Psychometrics of the Revised Portrait Value Questionnaire
papers.abstract_snippet: Validates PVQ-RR across 49 cultural groups (N=53,472) and 32 languages. Reliably measures 15 of 19 values in vast majority of groups. Perfectly reproduces theorized circular order of 19 values via MDS. Establishes configural and metric measurement invariance across groups.

papers.title: An Overview of the Schwartz Theory of Basic Values
papers.venue: Online Readings in Psychology and Culture
papers.abstract_snippet: Accessible overview of the Schwartz value theory for cross-cultural psychology. Explains circular structure, motivational conflicts and compatibilities, 10 value types, and their empirical validation across cultures.

papers.title: Development in Judging Moral Issues
papers.abstract_snippet: Foundational monograph introducing the Defining Issues Test (DIT) as a measure of moral judgment development based on Kohlberg's stages. Established the recognition paradigm for studying moral reasoning rather than production-based interview methods.

papers.title: A Neo-Kohlbergian Approach: The DIT and Schema Theory
papers.authors: James Rest, Darcia Narvaez, Stephen J. Thoma, Muriel J. Bebeau
papers.abstract_snippet: Proposes neo-Kohlbergian approach replacing Kohlberg's stages with moral schemas (Personal Interest, Maintaining Norms, Postconventional). Reformulates postconventional thinking and redefines cognitive structures as schemas rather than stages. Theoretical basis for the DIT-2.

papers.title: DIT2: Devising and Testing a Revised Instrument of Moral Judgment
papers.authors: James Rest, Darcia Narvaez, Stephen J. Thoma, Muriel J. Bebeau
papers.abstract_snippet: Introduces the DIT-2: revised for brevity, clarity, and more powerful validity criteria. Five moral dilemmas with rate-and-rank format. Takes 30-45 minutes. Improved validity indices and more contemporary dilemma scenarios compared to original DIT.

papers.title: Measuring Moral Thinking from a Neo-Kohlbergian Perspective
papers.abstract_snippet: Reviews measuring moral reasoning from the neo-Kohlbergian perspective. Discusses DIT/DIT-2 psychometric properties, schema theory underpinnings, and methodological advances in moral judgment measurement.

papers.title: Does Moral Education Improve Moral Judgment? A Meta-Analysis of Intervention Studies Using the Defining Issues Test
papers.authors: Andre Schlaefli, James R. Rest, Stephen J. Thoma
papers.abstract_snippet: Meta-analysis of 55 education intervention studies using the DIT. Dilemma discussion and psychological development programs produce modest overall effect sizes. Treatments of 3-12 weeks are optimal. Foundational meta-analysis for DIT validity evidence.

papers.title: Moral Reasoning Development: Norms for Defining Issue Test-2 (DIT2)
papers.abstract_snippet: Updated normative data for the DIT-2 after 14 years. Provides contemporary norms for moral reasoning development across educational levels. Essential for benchmarking DIT-2 results against current populations.

papers.title: Validity Study Using Factor Analyses on the Defining Issues Test-2 in Undergraduate Populations
papers.abstract_snippet: DIT-2 is a valid measure of internal structure of moral reasoning development using confirmatory factor analysis and bi-factor models. Validates the three-schema structure (Personal Interest, Maintaining Norms, Postconventional) in undergraduate populations.

papers.title: Modernization and Postmodernization: Cultural, Economic, and Political Change in 43 Societies
papers.abstract_snippet: Draws on World Values Surveys covering 70% of world population. Identifies two dimensions of cross-cultural variation: Traditional vs. secular-rational values and Survival vs. self-expression values. Economic development, cultural change, and political change follow coherent patterns.

papers.title: Assessing the Alignment of Large Language Models With Human Values for Mental Health Integration: Cross-Sectional Study Using Schwartz's Theory of Basic Values
papers.abstract_snippet: Administered PVQ-RR to 4 LLMs (Bard, Claude 2, GPT-3.5, GPT-4) and compared with 53,472 humans across 49 nations. Substantial divergence: all models prioritized universalism and self-direction while de-emphasizing achievement, power, and security relative to humans.

papers.title: Do LLMs Have Consistent Values?
papers.abstract_snippet: Applies 57-item PVQ-RR to LLMs. Standard prompting fails to produce human-consistent value correlations. Novel 'Value Anchoring' prompting strategy significantly improves alignment with Schwartz's circular model. Shows LLMs can generate coherent human-like value profiles with appropriate prompting.

papers.title: Probing the Moral Development of Large Language Models through Defining Issues Test
papers.abstract_snippet: Evaluates LLM moral reasoning via DIT. GPT-3 performs no better than random; GPT-4 achieves post-conventional moral reasoning equivalent to graduate students. ChatGPT, Llama2-Chat, PaLM-2 comparable to adult humans. Models inconsistent across dilemmas.

papers.title: Stages of Moral Judgment Development: Applying Item Response Theory to Defining Issues Test Data
papers.abstract_snippet: Applies Item Response Theory to DIT data to examine Kohlberg's stages of moral judgment development. Provides psychometric refinement of moral development measurement using modern measurement models.

papers.title: Cultural Value Alignment in Large Language Models: A Prompt-based Analysis of Schwartz Values in Gemini, ChatGPT, and DeepSeek
papers.abstract_snippet: Compares Schwartz value profiles of Gemini, ChatGPT, and DeepSeek using 40-item PVQ. DeepSeek uniquely downplays self-enhancement values compared to Western models, aligning with collectivist cultural tendencies. Self-transcendence highly prioritized across all models.

papers.title: Do Moral Judgment and Reasoning Capability of LLMs Change with Different Languages? A Study Using the Multilingual Defining Issues Test
papers.abstract_snippet: Critically assesses validity of methods for eliciting moral judgments from LLMs. Finds previous results confounded by biases in presentation of options in moral judgment tasks. Claude 3.5 Sonnet achieves highest post-conventional P-score of 72.
